exposure: Psychometric properties of the German version of the Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised (DE-BSS-R)
Mode of birth (non-instrumental vaginal, instrumental vaginal, caesarean section)
outcome: Known-groups discriminant validity of the DE-BSS-R
cohort: A total of 3747 German women participating in the INVITE cross-sectional study.
finding: The German cross-cultural adaptation of the Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised (DE-BSS-R) demonstrated excellent psychometric properties, making it a valid tool to measure birth satisfaction in German women.
mod_finding: Women who experienced a non-instrumental vaginal birth reported significantly higher birth satisfaction than women who had an instrumental birth (instrumental vaginal or caesarean section).
